subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be scoped to dropped-media diagnostics while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 owns configurable roots, or should this issue change the host-local media root contract itself?
rationale: The diagnostic improvement is narrow, but accepting more absolute host paths changes a file-read/upload security boundary and overlaps the broader root-policy design.

options.title: Diagnostics here, roots elsewhere
options.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level reason logging and optional user-visible attachment-unavailable feedback, while root expansion remains with the canonical root-policy item.

options.title: Adopt shared root policy here
options.body: Use this issue to define and implement the shared root contract, including schema, docs, Telegram delivery, and upgrade/security proof.

options.title: Document current behavior only
options.body: Close the expansion direction and document managed roots plus the CLI/media staging workaround without adding new runtime behavior.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics here, roots elsewhere
recommendation.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level reason logging and optional user-visible attachment-unavailable feedback, while root expansion remains with the canonical root-policy item.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant current history for outbound media roots and file-read policy points to this owner candidate.
